note: Faithful rendering of the Vinaya commentary on the building rule; the gloss on 'entirely' is loose but the obscure Tibetan allows it.

errors.english: He thoroughly knew the truth of recollection
errors.why: དྲན་པ here is smṛti, the traditional law books paired with the Vedas, not 'recollection'.

fix.find: He thoroughly knew the truth of recollection
fix.replace: He thoroughly knew the truth of the (smṛti) traditional law books

errors.english: equal to the immortal master and teacher of the gods
errors.why: The compound is 'the guru of the lord of the immortals' (Bṛhaspati, preceptor of Indra), not 'the immortal master and teacher of the gods'.
This is the jātaka narrative formula anuśrūyate 'it is told/handed down', not the sūtra formula evaṃ mayā śrutam.

note: Content is broadly followed, but the opening verses are flattened into prose and the description of the Brahmin learning misreads two standard terms.

errors.english: or from which arising does not occur
errors.why: In this list (no buddha-qualities, no awakening, no path, no liberation) འབྱུང་བ is deliverance/going forth (niryāṇa), not 'arising'; the same misreading recurs in 'understood the source of all phenomena'.

note: A sound rendering of the Madhyamaka argument and the Akṣayamatinirdeśa quotation, with one doubtful term.

errors.english: or those that have not been rendered permissible for mouth consumption
errors.why: ཁྱེའུ་ཁ་འཐོན་པ are sprouted shoots whose tips have emerged; 'not made allowable' (kalpika) has nothing to do with the mouth or eating.

fix.find: or those that have not been rendered permissible for mouth consumption
fix.replace: or sprouted shoots, that have not been made allowable (kalpika)

errors.english: down to their very root system
errors.why: ཐ་ན…ཡན་ཆད sets a minimum: damaging even so little as a root fibre counts, not destroying them thoroughly down to the roots.

note: The plant lists and the definition of pātayantika are fine, but the operative rule's description of the protected object is garbled.
Accurate translation of the five modes of Prātimokṣa recitation and the reciter's and elder's duties.

errors.english: But this is not the case; if it were possessing parts
errors.why: དེ་ལྟ་མ་ཡིན་ཏེ here means 'otherwise' (if it were not partless), supporting the preceding claim; 'this is not the case' reads as denying it.

note: A good rendering of the atom-and-arrangement argument against the Vaiśeṣika, with one connective that blurs the argument.
Careful, literal rendering of the commentary on mantra efficacy that tracks the argument and the lemmata correctly.

errors.english: whatever is the cause and whatever is the condition for alteration
errors.why: འགྱུར་བ completes སེམས་ཅན་རྣམས་ཀྱི་རྣམ་པར་དག་པར་ from the previous side: the cause and condition for beings' becoming purified, not 'alteration'.

fix.replace: the condition for sentient beings' becoming completely purified

note: Faithful rendering of the sūtra passage on causes, conditions and the Tathāgata's absorptions, apart from the cross-boundary opening.

errors.english: To anticipate an objection regarding perception
errors.why: རྟོགས་པ is understanding/cognizing the universal, not perception (pratyakṣa); the same slip produces 'Perception is the universal' below.

errors.english: that are being excluded [note: original: བསལ་བ་, Sanskrit: apoha
errors.why: In context (how many individuals must be seen; next side: not all individuals) བསལ་བ stands for གསལ་བ 'individual/manifest', and the apoha note is misleading.

note: The lemma-by-lemma structure is followed, but several glosses on cognition and individuals mislead in an already terse commentary.

errors.why: With སྔར་ཡང་ from the previous side this is ཡང་དག་པར་ནི་བསྟན་པ 'has been properly/correctly shown', glossed as 'stated clearly'; nothing is 'purified'.

errors.english: for since a definite effect is seen at all times, it is to be inferred.
errors.why: The whole argument from གལ་ཏེ to ཕྱིར་རོ is the anticipated objection introduced by 'But the effect…', yet the English presents its first part as the commentator's own assertion.

note: Close and mostly careful construal of a difficult commentary, but it misreads the cross-boundary opening and mis-scopes one objection.
